key_insight: A two-stage contrastive training pipeline — first mining large-scale, diverse weak signals then refining with graded relevance — produces embeddings that better separate exact matches, substitutes, complements and negatives for multi-category e‑commerce search.
problem_solved: Scalable production-ready embeddings that capture graded relevance in noisy, long-tail e‑commerce queries while respecting product and policy constraints, improving retrieval beyond binary relevance labels.
method: Mine: gather large-scale weak/pseudo supervision from production signals and heuristics to capture diverse candidate positives (substitutes, complements, noisy matches).
Refine: contrastive fine-tuning using graded relevance (multi-level labels or sampled margins) to explicitly separate exact matches, acceptable substitutes/complements, and negatives.
Production-aware training: incorporate hard negatives, sampling strategies and policy/product filters to keep supervision scalable and compliant for deployment.
impact: Delivers more robust, production-ready embeddings that improve retrieval quality across head and long-tail queries and enable better ranking/UX in e‑commerce systems; applicable to other domains needing graded relevance.

paper_title: Mine and Refine: Optimizing Graded Relevance in E-commerce Search Retrieval
paper_authors: Jiaqi Xi, Raghav Saboo, Luming Chen, Martin Wang, Sudeep Das
